running this simple curl command on your host:
$ curl -H 'accept: application/json' -X 'GET' 'http://localhost:

Token context window: Enter the value for the maximum number of tokens
(roughly words/subword units) that the model can "see" at once. You can start
with a conservative 4096 value and increase later if necessary.
Figure 15.23: The AnythingLLM model configuration screen, showing the custom LLM settings filled
in
Complete the idx_73422bd5 setup. You will be taken to the main chat interface.
Step 4: Testing your personal assistant
You are now ready to interact idx_3cc243ff with your fully private, locally-hosted chatbot.
First of all, select the first created workspace through the left navigation bar. Then, try asking a
question, such as What is Podman?. The request will travel from the AnythingLLM container
to your local inference server container, be processed by the AI model, and the response will be
streamed back to the web interface.

chunks.heading: 4.501 Managing Your Container, Kubernetes, and AI Workloads from a Graphical Interface
chunks.sectionTitle: Managing Your Container, Kubernetes, and AI Workloads from a Graphical Interface
chunks.content:
4.501 Managing Your Container, Kubernetes, and AI Workloads from a Graphical Interface
To confirm that the entire stack is running as expected, return to Podman Desktop and
navigate to the Containers list. You should now see at least two running containers: your AI
inference server and your web application (anythingllm).
Figure 15.24: The final AnythingLLM application container querying the AI model server
With that, you have successfully built and deployed a sophisticated, end-to-end AI application
without leaving the Podman Desktop interface. This demonstration shows the immense power
of combining containerization with modern AI, enabling developers to innovate, experiment,
and build the next generation of intelligent applications right from their own workstation.
Summary
With that, we have concluded our exploration of managing containers and advanced
workloads through a graphical interface. This chapter demonstrated how Podman Desktop
serves as a comprehensive and user-friendly control center, bridging the gap between the
power of the command line and the accessibility of a GUI.
First, we walked through the necessary prerequisites, detailing the step-by-step installation of
Podman Desktop on various operating systems, including Linux, macOS, and Windows. We
then delved into its core capabilities for local container management, learning how to easily
pull images, run and stop containers, and inspect their logs and internal state. We also
explored how to configure persistent storage using volumes and manage network access
through simple port mapping, all without writing a single command.

chunks.title: podmanfordevopssecondedition
chunks.heading: Chapter 15 502
chunks.content:
Chapter 15 502
Building on these fundamentals, we extended our reach to orchestrated environments. We
learned how to connect Podman Desktop to a Kubernetes cluster, transforming it into a
powerful client for managing remote workloads. We saw how to browse and interact with
essential Kubernetes resources such as Pods, Deployments, and Services, providing a single
pane of glass for both local development and production-like environments.
Finally, we ventured into the exciting world of AI with Podman AI Lab. We introduced this
innovative feature, enabled it, and used it to provision a local, containerized AI inference server
with just a few clicks. The culmination of our journey was the creation of a complete, end-to-
end personal chatbot. By integrating our locally running AI model with the containerized
AnythingLLM application, we demonstrated how Podman Desktop can orchestrate a full
application stack, proving that complex, AI-driven use cases are now well within the reach of
every developer, right on their own machine. This chapter's journey showcased the evolution
of container management tools to embrace not only orchestration but also the next frontier of
AI-powered development.
This book's journey finishes here, but Podman's amazing evolution continues thanks to its
growing adoption in many contexts and its vibrant and helpful community.
Before you move on, don't forget to join the community on IRC, Matrix, or Discord and
subscribe to the relevant mailing lists. Feel free to ask for and give feedback, and contribute to
help with the growth of the project.
Thank you for your interest and dedication.
